Guidance & outlook: FY 2025 has been a year of significant operational and market headwinds, with revenue of ₹ 3812.85 lakhs and net Loss of ₹ 49.16 lakhs reflecting the challenging conditions that affected the broader Indian seed industry during the season - including erratic monsoon pat- terns, compressed cotton acreage in key geographies, and pricing pressures across several…

The India seed market is estimated at USD 3.82 billion in 2025 and is expected to reach USD 5.01 billion by 2030, at a CAGR of 5.56%, driven by growing hybrid adoption across maize, vegetables, and rice - segments that demonstrated resilience even as cotton seed volumes contracted.
In FY 2025-26, the cotton segment recorded revenue of ₹ 1265 Lakhs.
Growth & demand: India's cotton acreage declined approximately 3% to 11.4 million hectares for MY 2025-26, driven by a farmer shift toward more profitable crops such as pulses and oilseeds - a pattern that directly compressed cotton hybrid seed demand for the season.

While the move benefited mills and exporters, it flooded the domestic market with cheaper imported cotton, curbing local mill demand and driving seed cotton prices approximately 16% below the revised MSP , necessitating large-scale government intervention through CCI procurement across 570 centres in 149 districts.

Unapproved HTBT cotton cultivation - driven by farmers seeking to save ₹7,000-8,000 per acre in manual weeding costs and address pink bollworm resistance - now covers an estimated 20% or more of India's total cotton acreage, directly harming the legitimate seed industry by displacing registered BG-II hybrid demand without any quality or accountability guaran…
Margins & costs: The central government announced a complete waiver of the 11% customs duty and Agriculture Infrastructure and Development Cess on raw cotton imports effective August 19, 2025, citing raw material cost pressures on the textile sector .
